nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What shortcomings exist in current studies regarding the thermal environment of rural minority housing?
nodes.answer: Some studies only consider certain factors affecting the indoor thermal environment without comprehensively analyzing all relevant factors, and there is a need for deeper research on the thermal insulation performance and properties of building materials.
nodes.paragraph: Li24 proposed that in the Lhasa plateau area, the near-zero energy heating of rural residential buildings can be realized by adopting efficient passive design methods. The results can be used as a guide for energy-saving design of rural residential buildings in plateau solar radiation areas in severe cold regions of China. Studying the energy consumption and thermal comfort of traditional dwellings of ethnic Scientific Reports minorities can not only improve the quality of life of residents, protect and inherit ethnic minority culture, but also promote technological innovation, energy conservation, and emission reduction, promote the sustainable development of the construction industry, and contribute to the construction of a better and more livable living environment25 29. Although scholars from all over the world have actively explored the energy conservation and emission reduction of traditional houses, there are few studies on the energy consumption of traditional houses of rural ethnic minorities compared with those of urban houses, and there are some limitations and shortcomings. The above study21 mentions the use of quantitative methods for analysis but lacks an in-depth understanding of the actual situation of rural minority housing. Some studies23 only consider the influence of some factors on the indoor thermal environment but do not comprehensively and accurately consider other factors, and the research on the thermal insulation performance of traditional residential envelope structures and the thermal properties of building materials still needs to be deepened.

nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What methods were used to collect data on the indoor thermal environment of traditional houses in the study?
nodes.answer: Field measurements and questionnaire surveys were used to collect data on indoor temperature, humidity, airflow velocity, and the temperature of each wall of the envelope structure.
nodes.paragraph: Some studies22 focus on the problems and deficiencies in the design of residential buildings, such as building orientation, materials, roof design, etc. However, no specific measures were provided on how to improve these design issues, etc. In addition, there is a relative lack of interdisciplinary cooperation and exchange, which leads to the one-sidedness and limitations of the research results. There is a lack of research on the traditional dwellings of ethnic minorities in the Sichuan Plateau. Due to the complexity of the natural environment, regional cultural differences, and local cultural traditions, there are relatively few empirical studies on building energy consumption, and the construction level of human settlements lags significantly behind that of other regions. Therefore, this study aims to fill this knowledge gap, gain an in-depth understanding of the actual situation of ethnic minority residential buildings in the Sichuan Plateau through field investigation and analysis, and propose energy-saving measures to adapt to the local area, so as to provide guidance for the sustainable development of local ethnic minority residential buildings. In this study, we obtained first-hand data on the indoor thermal environment of the traditional houses of ethnic minorities in the Sichuan Plateau, including indoor temperature, humidity, airflow velocity, and the temperature of each wall of the envelope structure, through field measurements and questionnaire surveys.

nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What is the functional unit used in the comparative assessment of insulation materials by Schmidt et al. (2004a, b) and Schulte et al. (2021)?
nodes.answer: The functional unit used in their comparative assessment is thermal resistance.
nodes.paragraph: Standard construction practices are still reliant on products made from fossil-based resources, especially for insulation materials. Insulation materials manufactured from bio-based resources have emerged as an alternative to the more tradi- tional fossil-based insulations. Bio-based insulations have the advantage of using renewable resources, if produced under environment-friendly practices, can store carbon (Lawrence et al. 2013) and, if not recyclable, can sometimes be used for soil conditioning (Beigbeder et al. 2019). Several studies have found lower environmental impacts for some bio-based material (Schmidt et al. 2004a; Murphy and Norton 2008; Pargana et al. 2014; Schulte et al. 2021; Carcassi et al. 2022). Schmidt et al. (2004a, b) and Schulte et al. (2021) compared the environmental impact of plant- based insulation materials to conventional materials. Both Schmidt et al. (2004a, b) and Schulte et al. (2021) performed a cradle-to-grave life cycle assessment (LCA) and compared the materials using thermal resistance as the functional unit. Products were compared by investigating all the environ- mental impacts prescribed in International Standard Organi- zation (1997).

nodes.question: What does the incorporation of highly conductive fillers alter during Frontal Polymerization (FP)?
nodes.answer: It alters the thermal transport characteristics during FP, potentially allowing heat from the polymerization reaction to advance ahead of the front into the unreacted monomer.
nodes.paragraph: The efficacy of heat trans - port through the unpolymerized medium is determined by the thermal conductivity and heat capacity of the reaction media [ 4]. Furthermore, boundary condition effects like heat loss to the surrounding medium can have a significant influence, i.e., can alter the thermal equilibrium between the heat generated by the exothermic reaction and the heat consumed by the advancing front [ 4, 5]. Motivated by the substantial energy and time savings offered by the FP approach, com - pared to conventional manufacturing techniques, more advances have been made in the development and usage of this technique for the rapid fabrication of reinforced, highly filled polymer composites [ 2, 4, 6 9]. Fig. 1 Principle of Thermal Frontal Polymerization (TFP) 13 Applied Composite MaterialsBesides the fact that the purpose of the fillers is clearly to modify the properties of the composite (e.g., improve mechanical properties, reduce the coefficient of thermal expan - sion, a.s.o.) another effect of fillers can be identified, namely the effect of the filler on the curing behavior (i.e., the thermal transport characteristics as well as curing kinetics).

nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How does the addition of highly conductive fillers affect the curing behavior and thermal transport in thermal frontal polymerization?
nodes.answer: The addition of highly conductive fillers alters the thermal transport characteristics during polymerization, leading to increased energy dissipation and reduced availability of exothermic energy as the volume fraction of resin decreases with increasing filler content.
nodes.paragraph: Further efforts to study the effects of added fillers (glass, steel, carbon) include the publications of Kumar et al. [ 6] who presented analytical expressions for the velocity of the self-propagating reaction front in the FP of thermoset polymers and composites, Vyas et al. [10] who presented a numerical study of the manufacturing of unidirectional glass-fiber- reinforced composites via FP, Wang et al. [ 9] who investigated the effect of fiber volume fraction on the average front velocity and the maximum temperature in the FP process, and Centellas et al. [ 10] who investigated the effect of multiple polymerization fronts on the composite cure time, quality, and mechanical performance. However, the detailed investi - gation of the influence of different filling degrees (in particular with respect to composites with high filling degrees on inorganic particles) using mathematical modeling & numerical simulation routines, is still in its infancy. With respect to curing kinetics, publications are either based on the determination of cur - ing kinetics of the unfilled resin, ignoring the influence of the filler content on curing kinet - ics, e.g., by Wang et al.

nodes.question: How does the presence of fillers, like Fe3O4 nanoparticles, affect the heat generation and thermal transport in the polymerization process?
nodes.answer: The presence of fillers reduces the available resin content, which leads to a decrease in heat generation, while the fillers also absorb some heat, resulting in a decline in frontal velocity and temperature with increasing filler content.
nodes.paragraph: [ 11] and Centellas et al. [ 8] or provide a systematic experimental investigation of the influence of predefined filler content and/or filler shape on curing kinet - ics [12 14]. However, no studies on studies on Bisphenol A Diglycidyl Ether (BADGE) with different filling degrees of Fe3O4 nanoparticles can be found in literature. In this study, Fe3O4 nanoparticle fillers were added to a Bisphenol A Diglycidyl Ether (BADGE) resin system that frontally polymerized through a Radical-Induced Cationic Frontal Polymerization (RICFP) mechanism. The nano-size Fe3O4 is an attractive material due to its unique characteristic properties such as superparamagnetism, low toxicity, high surface to volume ratio, easy synthesis, and biocompatibility [ 15]. An application field of such magnetic composite materials is electromagnetic shielding, which aims at reducing the electromagnetic field in defined areas. The detailed compilation of fundamental material and their subsequent usage in Modeling & Simulation routines is expected to be a major contribution in the investigation of the various parameters that influence the dynamic phe - nomenon of FP and can support process optimization.
